perinatal asphycia produces changes in NOS in neuronal cells in the striatum and in endothelial cells of striatum and cortex.

the role of NO as a mediator of neuronal injury following perinatal hypoxia.
the role of nitric oxide in the pathogenesis of perinatal asphysia.
the effects of perinatal asphysia on nitric oxide (NO) synthase activity.

the hypothermic treatment is a neuroprotective strategy against perinatal asphycia.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypothermia inhibits the neuronal injury by decreasing the inappropriate activation of NADPH-d in endothelial cells and by inhibiting the NADPH-d reactivity in striatal and neocortical neurons.

hypothermic treatment reduces NOS activity in neuronal and vascular endothelial cells and prevents the neuronal loss in the striatum and the neocortex of newborn rats subjected to severe perinatal asphycia.

NOS activation is a key event in the pathogenesis of brain injury in asphyctic newborns.
hypothermia may be a valuable therapeutic tool to treat asphyctic brain injury.
